Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators were found. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided text shows no evidence of .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, install-time setup.py execution, PEP 517 build hooks, or interpreter-start execution.
  • The package contains logic where mem-mesh install writes Claude/Cursor/Kiro hook scripts and settings, but this is a documented user-invoked installer feature, not evidence of automatic execution during package installation or import.
  • Normal CLI/server behavior and IDE hooks that require explicit user activation were not classified as malicious automatic execution.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • **Credential harvesting:** The code checks and reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, masking it in diagnostics and using it for the enhanced Anthropic API hook. This appears to be one documented application credential. There is no evidence of broad harvesting of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, or registry tokens.
  • **Exfiltration/staging:** Calls to api.anthropic.com and localhost:8000 curl requests appear consistent with LLM analysis and local API storage functionality. No attacker-controlled C2, raw IP endpoint, paste/drop service, archive staging, or upload of harvested files was identified.
  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, launch agents, shell profile modification, self-reinstall logic, or OS-level persistence. IDE hook installation appears to be an explicit product feature.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes abuse, Docker socket access, cloud metadata access, CI/GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** No evidence of base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec loaders or obfuscated staged payloads. The pre-scan “encrypted-payload” matches appear to be conversation truncation/summary string handling, not malicious loader evidence.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on the provided files, there is no evidence of hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, sudden dependency insertion, typosquatting, or wheel/sdist mismatch.
  • The documented curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh appears to be uv installation guidance, not an automatically executed downloader during package installation.

Further Verification Needed

  • The input contains selected text from 16 files out of 316 total files. Full file contents, pyproject.toml entry points and build backend, sdist-vs-wheel comparison, and a diff against the upstream GitHub source should be reviewed for stronger assurance.
  • The provided corpus is insufficient to fully verify large/binary files or hidden files in the artifact.
